page: Amazon Web Services c7g.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by AWS ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 processors on the arm64 architecture, managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance provides 48 dedicated physical cores with a one-to-one thread-per-core mapping running at 2.6 GHz. It includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. System memory totals 96.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio typical of compute-focused platforms. The instance features no discrete graphics accelerators and contains no local storage, requiring external network-attached storage for persistent disk I/O over its 22 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark results reveal strong multi-threaded compute capability and robust memory throughput. PassMark memory testing registers in the top 10%, while uncached memory bandwidth reaches 271.87 GB/sec for read operations and 116.04 GB/sec for write operations. Multi-core performance is confirmed by a Geekbench multi-core score of 19,156.0 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 73,470.33, with strong execution in software compilation using Clang and ray tracing. In contrast, single-threaded metrics, including single-core Geekbench and compression utilities, sit in the middle 50% performance bracket, reflecting standard single-thread clock speeds on ARM architecture.

Because the platform provides 48 dedicated physical cores rather than shared simultaneous multithreading threads, it maintains consistent execution across concurrent processes. The instance processes 76.41 million Redis SET operations per second and sustains static web serving throughput of 63.56 GB/sec. In qualitative terms, the high core density of ARM silicon yields efficient compute and memory bandwidth per allocated resource unit. The primary operational tradeoff involves the complete absence of local NVMe drives, meaning high-IOPS storage demands rely entirely on network storage performance.

Amazon Web Services c7g.12xlarge is positioned for horizontally scalable and parallelized server tasks. Key application fits include high-concurrency web serving, CI/CD software compilation clusters, in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, and distributed microservices.

Configured without simultaneous multithreading, each of the 48 vCPUs corresponds to a physical core, supported by 96.0 GB of system memory and 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance omits local NVMe storage and GPUs, relying on a 22 Gbps baseline network link for external storage and communication. Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core processing in Clang compilation and ray tracing, paired with top-tier memory bandwidth. In-memory data operations excel, evidenced by 76.41 million Redis SET operations per second and 63.56 GB/sec static web throughput. Single-core performance remains in average ranges. The server provides efficient core density for parallelized workloads, making it well suited for continuous integration pipelines, web serving fleets, distributed caching layers, and containerized backends.
